review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment read, all 66 units including the table, title and deck. Eleven local corrections and one omitted deck sentence recorded.

changes.before: Laozi 31: weapons are instruments of ill omen, not the instruments of a gentleman; he uses them only when he cannot do otherwise, and holds calm restraint the highest. Chapter 30 runs the same way: he who assists a ruler with the Way does not coerce the world with arms — such affairs are apt to rebound. The Sima Fa, Renben: so if killing men brings peace to men, killing is permissible; if attacking a state is out of love for its people, attacking is permissible; if war stops war, then even war is permissible. The Mozi, Against Offensive Warfare III, answering the challenge that Yu, Tang and King Wu all campaigned and all became sage kings: you have not examined the class of my words, nor understood their reason. Those were not what is called attack; they are called chastisement. And SAE's Theorem One: cannot-not — the carrier of cultivation is breached, and cultivation in a gentler form can no longer continue.
changes.after: Laozi 31: weapons are instruments of ill omen, not the instruments of a gentleman; he uses them only when he cannot do otherwise, and holds calm restraint the highest. changes.before: All four refuse to treat war as an ordinary policy option, and each builds a condition of permission out of attitude, purpose, norm and structure. The overlap is real, and it is narrower than it looks. What the four share: none accepts advantageous, therefore permissible; all require an extra gate before war begins; and all place that gate high in their own system — Laozi in the two chapters on arms, the Sima Fa in its opening paragraph, Mozi across three whole chapters, SAE at Theorem One.
changes.after: All four refuse to treat war as an ordinary policy option, and they build their respective conditions of permission out of attitude, purpose, norm and structure. The overlap is real, and it is narrower than it looks. What the four share: none accepts advantageous, therefore permissible; all require an extra gate before war begins; and all place that gate high in their own system — Laozi in the two chapters on arms, the Sima Fa in its opening paragraph, Mozi across three whole chapters, SAE at Theorem One.
changes.reason: Keep the four distinct grounds, not an apparent claim that each tradition uses all four.

changes.before: What the four do not share is the character of that gate. Reading all four as the precondition every other road has been walked does not hold. Laozi: uses them only when he cannot do otherwise — a last-resort condition indeed. SAE: the carrier breached, the gentler form no longer possible — a last-resort condition indeed. The Sima Fa: killing that brings peace is permissible, war that stops war is permissible — this is a condition of justification. It does not ask whether other roads have been walked; it asks what this war serves. A war serving the ending of war is permitted by this reason even if other roads remain. The Mozi: those are not attack, they are chastisement — this is a condition of standing. It does not ask whether other roads have been walked; it asks which class this campaign falls into. Chastisement need not first show that the roads other than chastisement are exhausted.
changes.after: What the four do not share is the character of that gate. Reading all four as the precondition every other road is exhausted does not hold. The Sima Fa: killing that brings peace is permissible, war that stops war is permissible — this is a condition of justification. It does not ask whether other roads have been walked; it asks what this war serves. A war serving the ending of war is permitted by this reason even if other roads remain. The Mozi: those are not attack, they are chastisement — this is a condition of standing. It does not ask whether other roads have been walked; it asks which class this campaign falls into. Chastisement need not first show that the roads other than chastisement are exhausted.
changes.reason: The source says the other paths cannot lead through, not merely that they have been tried.

changes.before: The argument of Against Offensive Warfare I is an analogy. A man enters another's orchard and steals his peaches and plums, and all condemn him; killing an innocent man, stripping him of his clothes, taking his spear and sword, is more unrighteous still than taking another's horse or ox, because the injury to others is greater. In such cases the gentlemen of the world all know to condemn it. Yet when it comes to the great unrighteousness of attacking a state, they do not know to condemn it; they follow along and praise it and call it righteous. Can this be called knowing the distinction between righteous and unrighteous? The structure is clear: unrighteousness increases with the injury done — and this is an inconsistency in logic, not a divergence in values. Mozi presses it to the extreme: killing one man is one capital crime, killing a hundred a hundred; while attacking a state kills by the ten thousand and is called righteous — seeing a little black one calls it black, seeing much black one calls it white. That is not a difference in values but an inability to tell black from white.
changes.after: The argument of Against Offensive Warfare I is an analogy. A man enters another's orchard and steals his peaches and plums, and all condemn him; killing an innocent man, stripping him of his clothes, taking his spear and sword, is more unrighteous still than taking another's horse or ox, because the injury to others is greater. In such cases the gentlemen of the world all know to condemn it. Yet when it comes to the great unrighteousness of attacking a state, they do not know to condemn it; they follow along and praise it and call it righteous. Can this be called knowing the distinction between righteous and unrighteous? The structure is clear: unrighteousness increases with the injury done — and this is an inconsistency in logic, not a divergence in values. Mozi presses it to the extreme: killing one man is called unrighteous and incurs one capital penalty; killing a hundred is a hundredfold unrighteousness and incurs a hundred capital penalties; while attacking a state kills by the ten thousand and is called righteous — seeing a little black one calls it black, seeing much black one calls it white. That is not a difference in values but an inability to tell black from white.
changes.reason: Restore the parallel growth of unrighteousness and liability, which supports the consistency argument.

changes.before: There followed the simulated siege: Mozi unfastened his belt to make a wall and used slips of wood for engines; Gongshu Ban deployed nine changes of siege machinery and Mozi repelled all nine — Gongshu Ban's engines were exhausted and Mozi's defence had margin to spare. Gongshu Ban said he knew how to defeat him but would not say it; Mozi said he knew it too, and would not say it either. Asked the meaning, Mozi answered: Gongshu's intent is nothing more than to kill me. Kill me, and Song will be unable to hold and can be attacked. But my disciple Qin Huali and three hundred others already hold my defensive implements upon the walls of Song, awaiting the invaders from Chu. Though you kill me, you cannot cut them off.
changes.after: There followed the simulated siege: Mozi unfastened his belt to make a wall and used slips of wood for engines; Gongshu Ban deployed nine changes of siege machinery and Mozi repelled all nine — Gongshu Ban's engines were exhausted and Mozi's defence had margin to spare. Gongshu Ban said he knew how to defeat him but would not say it; Mozi said he knew it too, and would not say it either. Asked the meaning, Mozi answered: Gongshu's intent is nothing more than to kill me. Kill me, and Song will be unable to hold and can be attacked. But three hundred of my disciples, including Qin Huali, already hold my defensive implements upon the walls of Song, awaiting the invaders from Chu. Though you kill me, you cannot cut them off.
changes.reason: Restore the total of three hundred rather than three hundred plus Qin Huali.

changes.before: Preparing the City Gates makes the internal condition of a community a necessary condition of a city's defensibility, isomorphic with §11 of the treatise. Of the fourteen, walls, moats, towers, implements, grain and terrain are material conditions; while officials and people in accord, the ruler trustworthy and just and the myriad people delighting in him without end, the graves of fathers and mothers are there, deep resentment against the enemy and great merit toward one's superiors, rewards clear and credible and punishments severe enough to be feared — these are conditions internal to the community. This is deepening cultivation is national strength in Warring States form — whether a community can hold itself depends on its internal condition, not on how good a technician it has hired.
changes.after: Preparing the City Gates makes the condition of subjects within the community a necessary condition of a city's defensibility, isomorphic with §11 of the treatise. Of the fourteen, walls, moats, towers, implements, grain and terrain are material conditions; while officials and people in accord, the ruler trustworthy and just and the myriad people delighting in him without end, the graves of fathers and mothers are there, deep resentment against the enemy and great merit toward one's superiors, rewards clear and credible and punishments severe enough to be feared — these are conditions internal to the community. This is deepening cultivation is national strength in Warring States form — whether a community can hold itself depends on its internal condition, not on how good a technician it has hired.
changes.reason: Restore 主体状态 rather than a generic internal condition; leave the contested classical phrase for source clarification.

changes.before: The Mohists' defence of cities satisfies the gate, but their interest lies at the level of a community's continued existence, not at the level of benefit. Mohism was a community with a definite doctrine, a definite organisation, a definite way of life; and that community's continuation required one condition — that there exist a number of independent small states, some of whose rulers were willing to listen and to employ them. In a world annexed to the end, that condition disappears. Mozi calculated this himself in Against Offensive Warfare II: of the states enfeoffed in antiquity, those destroyed by offensive war are beyond counting; Ju in the east was a very small state, wedged between great ones, and in the end perished. In a world where the small states have all been swallowed, Mohism has nowhere to go. So stopping attacks is not altruism; it is guarding one's own carrier — only that carrier is not property or territory but a world in which small states still exist and someone is still willing to hear a doctrine.
changes.after: The Mohists' defence of cities satisfies the gate, but their interest lies at the level of a community's continued existence, not at the level of benefit. Mohism was a community with a definite doctrine, a definite organisation, a definite way of life; and that community's continuation required one condition — that there exist a number of independent small states, some of whose rulers were willing to listen and to employ them. In a world annexed to the end, that condition disappears. Mozi calculated this himself in Against Offensive Warfare II: of the states enfeoffed in antiquity, those destroyed by offensive war are beyond counting; Ju in the east was a very small state, wedged between Qi and Yue, and in the end perished. In a world where the small states have all been swallowed, Mohism has nowhere to go. So stopping attacks is not altruism; it is guarding one's own carrier — only that carrier is not property or territory but a world in which small states still exist and someone is still willing to hear a doctrine.
changes.reason: Restore the two named states in the quotation.

changes.before: The consequence of this determination is that the sense of the gate is broader than first supposed: it does not require the intervening party to have material gains or losses at stake, only that the intervening party's carrier of cultivation genuinely depends on the outcome of the intervention. The contrary possibility must be stated. Read more strictly — requiring a direct, identifiable common interest between intervening and intervened — the Mohists do not satisfy it, and Theorem One would then determine that the practice closest to 15DD in pre-Qin China does not hold. This volume adopts the broad reading, on the ground that the strict reading would exclude all cross-community assistance, which is not what this gate exists to prevent. What it exists to prevent is deciding on others' behalf whether they should resist — and the Mohists left precisely that decision to the other side.

changes.before: This volume, like the rest of the series, keeps its correction records in the body: withdrawn propositions, narrowed claims and reductions are marked where they occurred rather than silently repaired. They are kept for a reason — a framework that requires cannot-not be questioned must be the first thing questioned, and a text that shows no sign of ever having erred gives its reader no way to judge how its determinations were reached.
changes.after: This volume, like the rest of the series, keeps its correction records in the body: withdrawn propositions, narrowed claims and reductions are marked where they occurred rather than silently repaired. unresolved_source_questions.finding: The classical phrase 畜积索怨于民，有大功于上 has divergent renderings among draft translations. Existing English supplies against the enemy, absent explicitly from the current Chinese prose; do not silently settle a textual interpretation without checking the classical context.
The blanket assertion that all conscript armies lack internal review and appeal and make exit punishable by death may require qualification; preserved as source, not an approved change.
